title: Copper is flashing an AI warning sign, but China’s supply crunch may be telling a different story
excerpt: Copper is an economic bellwether, but it's also become an indicator of AI sentiment. The metal has slumped lately as the AI trade struggles.
content_html:
By Samuel O'Brient

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-28T10:50:01.259Z

A historically bearish economic indicator has been flashing in recent weeks: copper prices have plunged.

The industrial metal ended 2025 on track for its best year since 2009 but as 2026 winds down, the rally has fizzled. Adam Turnquist, chief cross asset strategist at LPL Financial recently noted, that copper has become another victim of the latest downswing across markets in the last month.

"Copper has stood apart this year in the broader metals complex as its fellow record-setting metals of gold, silver, and platinum rolled over," he wrote. "However, as market participants have worked their way through this month's equity market correction, what appeared to be another strong year for the red metal was quickly jeopardized."

Copper has been pulled down recently alongside the wider AI trade. A key component in data center construction, the metal drew considerable attention from the bullish tech investors pouring money into AI stocks while the bull rally continued through the first half of this year.

While copper prices surged, benefitting copper-linked stocks, some investors have expressed worries about a shortage that could compromise the AI buildout.

However, as concerns about massive capex spending from hyperscalers and their profit timelines mounted, and with the 2026 Democratic party's midterm elections sweep fueling anxiety about data center regulation, confidence in the AI trade has wavered, pull copper down along with other AI-linked assets.

Adding to the complexities in the metal market is China, which is the world's largest user of the metal.

"Chinese supplies have diminished as large volumes of London-traded copper have been redirected from China to the U.S. over the last two years aimed to front-run potential refined copper tariffs," he stated. "Add in a tight scrap market and Chinese smelters cutting production, and the result is Chinese inventories nearing their lowest levels since 2023."

Turnquist described the recent copper price action out of China as a "case study in contradiction," due to the combination of AI fears and concerns about China's economy slowing down, while the copper market itself tightens significantly.

Turnquist said that copper could be an indicator of how much investors believe in the AI boom, or if they expect to see the problems facing the data center buildout persist.

"The metal rebounded to start the week after NVIDIA's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, but if another wave of AI jitters washes over Wall Street, copper holding above its AI bull market trendline may be a behind-the-curtain key to AI sentiment," Turnquist said.
